en: Contrary to common belief, the Pasig River flows westward from Laguna de Bay into Manila Bay, not the other way around.
Many think Taal Volcano is on the mainland, but it is actually an island situated inside Taal Lake in Batangas.
While often mistaken as the largest, Lake Lanao is actually the second-largest lake in the Philippines, behind Laguna de Bay.
People often confuse the highest peaks, but Mount Pulag is the highest mountain in Luzon, not Mount Apo.
Although Mindanao is huge, its longest river is the Rio Grande de Mindanao, not the Cagayan River which is in Luzon.
Despite its location near the Visayas, Palawan is geographically part of the Luzon landmass, not the Visayas island group.
Some mistakenly believe Mount Mayon is in the Visayas, but this perfectly cone-shaped volcano is actually located in Albay, Luzon.
Contrary to popular belief, the Puerto Princesa Underground River flows into the South China Sea, not the Sulu Sea.
Even though it is in the Sulu Sea near the Visayas, the Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park belongs to Palawan province.
Many think the Sierra Madre mountain range is in Mindanao, but it is actually the longest mountain range located in Luzon.
Students often think the Philippine Sea is a separate ocean, but it is actually a marginal sea of the Pacific Ocean.
People assume the Chocolate Hills are volcanic, but they are actually formed from marine limestone deposits raised by tectonic forces.
